html:
SMTO-CFG-0031 — SMTO couldn't accept these Skill settings

GUID: 25a0ab9f-daaa-40e5-81eb-d85f55027e6e
Slug: skill-configuration-input-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • The Skill settings you tried to save or test are too large (over 64 KB) or contain a value in the wrong form. Nothing was saved, and no connection test ran.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Skill's settings window, check every field: fill in the required ones, and enter numbers, web addresses and choices in the form each field asks for. SMTO checks the whole form against the Skill's rules before testing or saving, and one wrong value stops both.
  2. For each credential, fill in both Parameter Store key and Credential field pointer. Don't paste a password or key directly into any field. Skills read secrets only through a reference to the Parameter Store, so a missing or half-filled reference is refused.
  3. Remove extra entries or very long pasted text, then select Test connection or Save again. SMTO refuses Skill settings larger than 64 KB, even when each value is correct.
  4. If you can't find the problem, select Reload saved configuration and make your changes again. This drops your unsaved edits and starts you from the last settings SMTO accepted.

What success looks like

  • Test connection shows a result message, or the window says "Saved. Future calls use this configuration."

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Skill's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't include passwords or keys in what you send.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Skill configuration route rejected the request body because it exceeded 64 KiB, was not valid JSON, or the connection-test candidate failed TestCandidate or Skill schema validation.

What this means

  • Skill configuration input exceeds 64 KiB, fails JSON/object parsing or cannot validate against the installed schema/test candidate contract. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Skill configuration input exceeds 64 KiB, fails JSON/object parsing or cannot validate against the installed schema/test candidate contract.

How to diagnose it

  • Check byte size, object shape and safe field errors against the installed configuration definition.

How to fix it

  • Send a JSON object of at most 65,536 bytes. A configuration/test body may contain only configuration (object) and provider_id (string, up to 80 characters), and the configuration must pass SkillConfigurationDefinition.validate (JSON schema, schema_version and Parameter Store references for secret fields). Without a candidate, the saved configuration must load; replace it with a valid PUT if it does not.
  • Use a valid JSON object matching the installed Skill schema, within 64 KiB. Supply credentials only through the Skill’s secure configuration fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded supported candidate validates before a configuration save or test.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
